extracted.intended_audience: agency ADP control officers, comptroller/management staff and officials responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-76 for government automated data processing (ADP) requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on implementing and complying with OMB Circular A-76 for government Automated Data Processing (ADP) requirements, including when to use commercial services, when to protect classified/sensitive information from outsourcing, and reporting/coordination procedures with the Comptroller and OMB examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use commercial services whenever possible
rubrics_metrics.description: We are in agreement with the general desire to use commercial services whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance in the draft transmittal memorandum appears in concert with our own general approach to ADP products; an analysis of the planned FY 1978 ADP program shows approximately 70 percent of ADP dollars go to commercial sources. This expresses a policy preference to rely on commercial providers where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularly consider contracting out when weighing alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: We regularly consider contracting out when weighing alternative methods of implementing our ADP programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating methods to implement ADP programs, contracting out should be a routine option in the decision process and be weighed against in-house alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect sources, methods, and sensitive information (limitation on outsourcing)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are required to protect our sources and methods, as well as sensitive information provided by other organizations. At times, therefore, we are precluded from using external services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National security, protection of intelligence sources/methods, or protection of sensitive third-party information may override the general preference for commercial services; where such protection is required, outsourcing is not permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue reporting and coordination with designated examiners and Comptroller
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to meet the spirit of the guidelines of Circular A-76, we plan to continua reporting directly to our OIS.IB Examiner on the matters covered by the circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination on the Agency's response to OMB's transmittal memorandum occurred with the Office of the Comptroller and action was transferred from ODP to the Comptroller. Maintain established reporting channels (e.g., to OMB examiners and the Comptroller) for matters under A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align agency ADP policy with the spirit of Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency concurs with the general desire expressed in the transmittal memorandum and finds the draft guidance to be in concert with its approach to ADP products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency ADP policy should be shaped to reflect the intent of A-76 (preference for commercial sourcing where feasible) while balancing unique agency constraints such as the need to protect sources and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and analyze ADP expenditures as evidence of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: An analysis of our planned FY 1978 ADP program shows that approximately 70 percent of our ADP dollars go to commercial sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and use expenditure analyses (e.g., percent of ADP dollars to commercial sources) as part of documentation demonstrating conformity with A-76 guidance and procurement decisions.
